Introduction:

The superior court of San Bernardino is a city courthouse serving the residents of San Bernardino County, California. It is located within the court of appeal in the fourth district, and the appeal from the central district goes to the ninth circuit United State Court of appeal. The courthouse was established in 1858 with a jail, then in 1878, the courthouse was shifted to a new place, then further replacements were made, and the latest courthouse that serves nowadays was built in 2014 with 35 courtrooms. The court's mission is to protect and preserve the rights of every person and provide justice and effective resolution to all the fights in this court. It has jurisdiction over criminal, small claims, probation, juvenile, appeal, civil, family, traffic, and vehicle matters. It also handles mental health problems cases. They provide online services like online payment, forms, fines, probate notes, juror status, and many more, so it is optional to go to court for these services. This court also provides self-help for a different division. Proper dressing is required during the court session, and wearing a mask is mandatory. In this article, we will provide an overview of the Superior Court of San Bernardino, its history, services, and procedures.

The Superior Court of San Bernardino is a state court, and it has jurisdiction over all civil and criminal cases in the county, excluding those cases that are within the exclusive jurisdiction of the federal courts. This court is responsible for handling a wide range of cases, including family law, probate, personal injury, small claims, misdemeanors, felonies, and juvenile cases.

How to search for cases?

San Bernardino courthouse judicial council case search can be done online through the court portal san bernardino justice center https://cap.sb-court.org/. The court maintains all the records online, in files, or in a database. They implemented enhanced services that remotely provide document images from case filing in civil matters. The case search can be done in the following ways:

  • Search by Case Number, citation, or traffic number
  • Search by First, middle, and last name
  • Search by Company name

After entering the data, the case information will come. The portal of san bernardino justice center will only show those records information that is publicly available. Some records are unavailable; if the information does not come, the case records will be removed, very old or confidential, and cannot be displayed online. You have to go to the court or give a record request for these documents, and then the court will decide whether to provide that information. If you want copies of any document, then $0.5 is the fee per page.

How to make a payment?

San Bernardino courthouse pay ticket and traffic ticket payment can be made in the following ways:

In-Person

A person can pay tickets and fines by visiting the court during regular court hours and paying in cash, checks, US funds, or a card at the court payment office. Take your ticket and case number with you when you come for payment. 2% surcharges will be applied if you make payment with a credit card.

Online

Online payments can be made using the Court portal https://cap.sb-court.org/. Search your case by entering any search type, like a case or traffic ticket number, or name. Your case information with the amount of the fine will be displayed. Select the payment option and pay the amount online. Convenience fees will be applied using this method.

Mail

A Person can send a certified check or money order to the court's mailing address, Superior Court of California, County of Bernardino, Attn: Financial Services BOX 15005 San Bernardino, CA 92415-5005 . Cash or personal checks are not acceptable in the mail; only certified checks or money orders are accepted. Remember to write your citation, name, case number, and account number when you send the payment, and mail the amount in a self-addressed, stamped envelope if you want a receipt.

Telephone

Payment can also be made by Telephone. Call (909) 481-4228 or (760) 241-9529 24 hours a day. Service charges will apply in this case. Traffic school sign-up, request for an extension on appearance date, and initial one-time extension can be made online or by phone.

How to appear remotely?

San Bernardino courthouse judicial council remote appearances for some eligible cases are possible using court calls, teams, and video conferencing in the zoom application. Fill out and send the form related to your case. The court will respond with a schedule and a meeting link ID for video conferencing if your case is eligible for the remote hearing. Make sure your internet connection is strong. Mute your microphone and speak only when the judge calls your name. Test your microphone and video before joining the session. It is recommended to avoid running unnecessary applications when you are in a meeting. Wear a proper dress and sit where your face is visible. Recording for the case hearing is not allowed. Recording for the case hearing is strictly not allowed. If you want a listen-in-only courtroom audio streaming, then this court is providing this facility with a touch-tone telephone or cellular device. You had to send a request at least five days before the schedule, and it must include the case number, party name, hearing date and time, courtroom and department, and the requestor's contact information. After providing the request, the court will respond. All division remote hearing detail instructions are available on the website; read them before giving a request.

The family law division handles which type of cases?

San Bernardino courthouse judicial council family law division handles many family cases and issues that include divorce, legal separation, nullity, guardianship, child custody, child support and visitation, domestic violence, elder abuse, adoptions, and many more. The information related to professional staff, the location of where to file the cases is available on the website. Which services are provided by the family court?

San Bernardino courthouse family court services are:

  • Mediation in which the court recommends counseling for child custody, support, guardianship and visitation.
  • Counseling for marital and relationship
  • Providing partial assessment for a juvenile who petitions the court according to the family code

They also provide online and in-person orientation facilities for child custody counseling, and for this, both parties had to complete the orientation for custody matters. The orientations were available in English and Spanish language.

How can a divorce case be filled?

San Bernardino courthouse divorce can be filed in the family law division. Divorce cases are complicated, and sometimes one person does not agree to the terms, so hiring or talking to the family lawyer or attorney is recommended before filing for the divorce. You can file a divorce by filing the divorce available at the clerk's office and online and providing some documents that the court requires. The case will only be filled if one of the couples lives in this county for at least 3 months and in California for at least 6 months. If the couple had a child, the child custody case would be filed with the divorce case. If you submit all the documents and both parties agree to some conclusion, divorce will be finalized after six months of the petition.

How can small claims cases be filled?

San Bernardino courthouse small claims court handles all the matters in which a person sues another person for money and personal damage within the limit of $10,000. For businesses, the limit is $5000. The cases can be resolved in quick, informal and inexpensive ways. Rules followed in these cases are very simple, and the hearing is informal. The case can be filled out by filling out the form available at http://www.courts.ca.gov/forms or by coming to the court in person, or by filling the form without any cost from http://turbocourt.com/. Fill in your and the defendant's personal information, the reason for your claim, and the amount you are suing. The cases can only be filled if the plaintiff's age is 18+; otherwise, the guardian must come with the minor. After the claim is filed, the court clerk will mail the defendant about the case and the schedule. The fees depend upon the amount of money you are claiming. The fee schedule contains all the information about the court fees. A small claims court commissioner, a temporary judge, or a judge can hear the case. You had to pay $15 to the clerk's court if you want certified mail with a receipt.

The traffic court handles which types of cases?

San Bernardino courthouse traffic court handles adult and minor traffic and vehicle violations, including speeding, parking ticket, driving without or with an expired license, and driving. At the same time, you have drugs, accidents, municipal code violations etc. If you received a traffic citation, many options are available for resolving it, and the court will mail you a reminder notice for your citation. You must appear on your schedule if the citation contains a mandatory appearance. You can choose any option for resolving the citation if a mandatory appearance is not required, but you must do it before the citation date. You can ask for a trial by sending a plea of not guilty to the court before the citation date. Some cases are solved by paying the fine online, but in case of correctable violation, you have to pay a fine with a proof correction. The traffic school option is available if your case is eligible for it. You had to fulfill the requirement for attending the traffic school.
